In [[mathematics]], particularly in [[functional analysis]], the '''Krein-Smulian theorem''' can refer to two theorems relating the closed [[convex hull]] and [[Compact space|compactness]] in the [[weak topology]]. They are named after [[Mark Krein]] and [[Vitold Shmulyan]], who published them in 1940.<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Krein|first1=M.|author1-link=Mark Krein|last2=Šmulian|first2=V.|author2-link=Vitold Shmulyan|doi=10.2307/1968735|journal=[[Annals of Mathematics]]|mr=2009|pages=556–583|series=Second Series|title=On regularly convex sets in the space conjugate to a Banach space|volume=41|year=1940|issue=3 |jstor=1968735 }}</ref>

==Statement==

Both of the following theorems are referred to as the Krein-Smulian Theorem.

{{math theorem|name=Krein-Smulian Theorem:{{sfn|Conway|1990|pp=159-165}}|note=|style=|math_statement=
Let <math>X</math> be a [[Banach space]] and <math>K</math> a weakly compact subset of <math>X</math> (that is, <math>K</math> is compact when <math>X</math> is endowed with the [[weak topology]]). Then the closed convex hull of <math>K</math> in <math>X</math> is weakly compact. 
}}

{{math theorem|name=Krein-Smulian Theorem{{sfn|Conway|1990|pp=159-165}}|note=|style=|math_statement=
Let <math>X</math> be a [[Banach space]] and <math>A</math> a convex subset of the continuous dual space <math>X^{\prime}</math> of <math>X</math>. If for all <math>r > 0,</math> <math>A \cap \left\{x^{\prime} \in X^{\prime} : \left\| x^{\prime} \right\| \leq r\right\}</math> is [[weak-star topology|weak-* closed]] in <math>X^{\prime}</math> then <math>A</math> is weak-* closed. 
}}
